title: Investigate cascading fallback to legacy-quant variant that triggered cross-region retry storm
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-10 a production routing policy caused a cascading fallback to an incompatible model variant (legacy-quant) which produced silent decode failures and triggered progressive cross-region reroutes and automated client retries. The event increased tail latency, doubled token costs for affected customers, and caused transient error rates to spike to ~12% for 18 minutes. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations applied, and tracked action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2026-03-10T09:12Z - First elevated error rates reported by SLO alerting for model-route api.chat.generate in us-central1.
2026-03-10T09:14Z - Observability flagged increased fallback rate: routing policy selected variant 'legacy-quant-v1' for ~11% of requests across multiple regions.
2026-03-10T09:16Z - Customer reports indicate malformed tokens and streaming disconnects; retries from SDKs began to increase.
2026-03-10T09:20Z - Automated retry logic + cross-region fallback logic produced a reroute loop between us-central1 and eu-west1 (approx. 3k requests/min oscillation).
2026-03-10T09:25Z - Engineering mitigation: disabled automatic fallback to legacy-quant in the policy engine and applied emergency route pin for primary variants.
2026-03-10T09:30Z - Disabled client-side automatic retry policy via config toggle for affected customers while rollbacks in progress.
2026-03-10T09:40Z - Error rates returned to baseline; full stabilization by 09:55Z after routing cache flush and rollback.
2026-03-10T12:00Z - Post-incident scrub scheduled; initial RCA drafted.
root_cause: Multiple factors combined: (1) A policy rule mistakenly matched on model family tag rather than exact compatibility profile, allowing fallback to 'legacy-quant-v1' despite incompatible tokenizer/byte-pair encoding differences. (2) The fallback selection did not mark variant as 'non-streaming-decoder-compatible', so streaming and response-decoding logic attempted to use the variant without conversion. (3) Automated client retry and cross-region fallback logic lacked a circuit-breaker for repeated variant-mismatch failures, producing a reroute loop between regions. (4) Observability lacked an immediate alert correlating fallback rate with decode-error class, which delayed root-cause identification by ~8 minutes.
mitigations:
Short-term: disabled legacy-quant fallback and applied route pinning; toggled client retry config for affected customers; flushed routing caches and cleared KV fallback caches to stop stuck policy state.
Medium-term: added an emergency circuit-breaker in routing engine to stop repeated cross-region reroutes for the same request trace; added metric and alert that correlates fallback-rate with decode-error classification.
Long-term: update variant compatibility model in policy engine so fallbacks require explicit compatibility flags; add preflight compatibility checks and stronger unit/integration tests around tokenization/streaming compatibility for model variants.
action_items: A1: Policy engine change - require explicit 'compatibility_profile' when selecting fallback variants; owner: @luca; due: 2026-03-20
A2: Add circuit-breaker to routing path to prevent repeated cross-region reroutes after N failures per trace; owner: @sofia; due: 2026-03-17
A3: Create integration tests that simulate mismatched tokenizer behavior and verify fallback is blocked; owner: @ryan; estimate: 3; due: 2026-03-24
A4: Observability - new alert that fires when fallback_rate > 1% AND decode_error_rate increases by >5x in 5m; owner: @marta; due: 2026-03-16
A5: Client SDK update - expose opt-out toggle for automatic retries and document guidance for backoff behavior; owner: @emily; due: 2026-03-28
A6: Run a tabletop incident rehearsal that exercises routing fallback and retry interactions; owner: @aisha; due: 2026-04-02
A7: Backfill variant metadata for all catalog entries to include streaming/decoder/tokenizer compatibility booleans; owner: @ops-team; due: 2026-03-31
